doc.title: Sheila Jordan interviewed by Monk Rowe, Middleburgh, New York, May 11, 2002

title: Kenny Barron and The Water Is Wide, from Fred Hersch
summary: They discuss The Water Is Wide, her work with Kenny Barron, and the song coming from Fred Hersch.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: And I thought oh my God isn’t that beautiful, that introduction.
Oh yeah that’s “Lost and Found.” Isn’t it?
Yeah but the name of the CD is “Lost and Found.”
Oh you don’t have the original.
I’m curious, do you think you could have sung this song to your satisfaction in 1962?
Yeah? That’s a nice change here.

Oh yeah. What I did was I modulated. I made the head arrangement modulating it. Yeah. I love Kenny Barron, he’s just so wonderful. We worked — I have a few albums with him. I have one in Japan that I did. But I’ve been working more with Steve now again after — we had our group together for a while and then that sort of didn’t make it and then so we recorded with different people. And then I went back to Ken again. I think
he’s so underrated. He’s such a beautiful player. But no, I like that song. Fred Hirsch gave me that song.
Fred Hirsch gave me that song.

It’s an old Scottish folk song. It’s an old, I think it’s Scottish. It’s either Scottish or British. I think it’s from Scotland though. I think so. And he played that for me. He said, “I have a song that I think you could really sing.” And he played it and he gave me a tape of him singing it and playing it and I started to cry. I said oh my God this is so beautiful. Actually on the back of the original that that’s on, “Lost and Found” I thanked him for giving me that.
